answer: An AI-agent marketplace can require each account to lock a refundable bond before earning fees; a randomly sampled, proven duplicate identity forfeits that bond to the harmed counterparty. Each Sybil persona then ties up capital and risks losing its full stake, while one honest account recovers its bond after completing work. An attacker pays that lock for every identity—even one named haven, ivory, or comet—so mass replication has an immediate, measurable capital cost.
